artifacts.notes: The first page of the Leonine Praefatio in Supplementum Tertiae Partis, unnumbered and signed 'SUMMAE THEOL. D. THOMAE T. IX.' at the foot. It carries the sentence dating the compilation to the middle of the fourteenth century and describing the Supplement as a second witness to the commentary on the Sentences, and the identification of the transcribed portion as beginning at book IV, distinction 14, question 1, article 3, quaestiuncula 2. Exact bytes are not retained in the repository.

artifacts.notes: Printed p. 205 of the Supplement, running head 'QUAESTIO LXXXVIII, ARTICULUS II, III'. It carries the end of q. 88 a. 1 corpus with its three replies, including the reply that distinguishes the twofold judgment owed to each man and calls the first 'unum singulare, quod de eo fiet post mortem'; the marginal apparatus cites 2 Cor 5:10. Articles 2 and 3 follow with their own parallel-place rubrics, and article 2's corpus concludes that what is said in Matthew 25 is probably to be understood as accomplished mentally and not vocally. The parallel-place rubric for article 1, which names Tertia Pars q. 59 a. 5 among its parallels, stands on the preceding page and is not shown here. Exact bytes are not retained in the repository.

work.author: Anonymous compiler; the Leonine editors name only the 'Compilator Supplementi'
work.description: The ninety-nine questions and two appendices printed after Aquinas's unfinished Tertia Pars to complete the Summa theologiae. It is a compilation, not an authorial work: the Leonine preface to the Supplement states that it was transcribed about the middle of the fourteenth century from some codex of Aquinas's commentary on the fourth book of the Sentences, and treats it as a second witness to that commentary's text rather than as a separate composition. The preface names its maker only as the Compilator, and identifies the transcribed portion as beginning at book IV, distinction 14, question 1, article 3, quaestiuncula 2. A widespread later attribution to Aquinas's socius Reginald of Piperno (died about 1290) appears in reference works and on the New Advent presentation, and cannot be reconciled with the Leonine dating without evidence this record does not have. It is registered as its own work so that its wording is never silently attributed to the Summa's author. The doctrine is Aquinas's own, from his earliest large systematic work; the arrangement, the article titles, and the text as printed are the compiler's. Questions 69-99 cover the state of souls after death, the resurrection, and the last judgment; the appendices cover limbo and purgatory. A locus is question.article.division, or appendix-N.question.article.division for the two appendices; the reserved locus 'preface' names the Leonine editors' Praefatio in Supplementum, which is editorial matter printed with this work rather than part of it.
work.title: Supplementum Tertiae Partis Summae theologiae
